title: Metabolic syndrome: a common problem among office workers
key_effect_estimate: MetS prevalence 35.9% (95% CI 33.5%-38.3%); lack of leisure-time physical activity p=0.003; low fruit intake p=0.02
interpretation: High MetS prevalence; inactivity and low fruit intake were associated with MetS

title: Work stress and metabolic syndrome in police officers. A prospective study
interpretation: Higher work stress predicted incident MetS

title: Leisure-time exercise, physical activity during work and commuting, and risk of metabolic syndrome
sample_or_followup: 22,383 workers; mean 4.1 years; 5,361 incident MetS cases
interpretation: Higher-intensity mixed leisure exercise associated with lower MetS incidence; commuting walking not associated

title: The relationship between physical activity levels and metabolic syndrome in male white-collar workers
key_effect_estimate: MetS prevalence 25.2% low PA, 13.9% moderate PA, 9.5% high PA for low-HDL criterion pattern; overall group differences p<0.001 for HDL-related component
interpretation: Higher physical activity corresponded to lower MetS/component prevalence

title: Sedentary Occupation Workers Who Meet the Physical Activity Recommendations Have a Reduced Risk for Metabolic Syndrome
key_effect_estimate: Active vs sedentary: MetS OR 0.52 (95% CI 0.27-0.98); abdominal obesity OR 0.36 (0.16-0.82); elevated BP OR 0.47 (0.26-0.84); low HDL OR 0.54 (0.31-0.93)
interpretation: Meeting PA recommendations was associated with lower MetS and component risk

title: The association of work-related stressors and their changes over time with the development of metabolic syndrome: The Furukawa Nutrition and Health Study
sample_or_followup: 1,040 manufacturing workers; 3 years; 61 incident MetS cases
interpretation: Increasing job demands over time associated with higher incident MetS

title: Telemonitoring-supported exercise training, metabolic syndrome severity, and work ability in company employees: a randomised controlled trial
main_caution: Allocation concealment/attrition details need final confirmation
key_effect_estimate: Between-group difference -0.26 (95% CI -0.35 to -0.16); p<0.0001
interpretation: Telemonitoring-supported exercise reduced MetS severity

title: Prevalence and lifestyle-associated risk factors of metabolic syndrome among commercial motor vehicle drivers in a metropolitan city in Ghana
key_effect_estimate: MetS prevalence 5%; tobacco use R=0.405 p=0.041; time of supper R=0.931 p=0.047
interpretation: MetS prevalence was low but selected lifestyle practices were associated with MetS

title: Metabolic syndrome among working adults in eastern Ethiopia
key_effect_estimate: Sedentary >=8 h: APR 2.29 (95% CI 1.88-2.80); >=5 fruit/veg servings: APR 0.04 (0.01-0.27)
interpretation: Sedentary time associated with higher MetS prevalence; high fruit/vegetable intake with lower prevalence

title: The influence of specific aspects of occupational stress on security guards' health and work ability
main_caution: Missing-data strategy needs final confirmation; overlaps Lifelines cohort
key_effect_estimate: Higher professional stressors positively predicted fasting glucose, triglycerides, total/LDL cholesterol, blood pressure and cardiovascular risk after adjustment
interpretation: Specific occupational stressors were associated with adverse metabolic and cardiovascular markers

title: Occupational distribution of metabolic syndrome prevalence and incidence differs by sex and is not explained by age and health behavior
main_caution: Missing-data strategy needs final confirmation; overlaps Lifelines cohort
key_effect_estimate: Men stationary plant/machine operators HR 1.94 (95% CI 1.26-3.00); women food-preparation assistants HR 1.80 (1.01-3.22)
interpretation: MetS risk differed by occupation and sex

title: Metabolic syndrome incidence in an aging workforce: Occupational differences and the role of health behaviors
main_caution: Attrition handling needs final confirmation; overlaps Lifelines cohort
key_effect_estimate: Low-skilled white-collar OR 1.24 (95% CI 1.12-1.37); low-skilled blue-collar OR 1.37 (1.18-1.59)
interpretation: Older low-skilled workers had higher incident MetS; behaviours explained part of differences

title: The association between job stress and metabolic syndrome among medical university staff
key_effect_estimate: Office workers OR 1.51 (95% CI 1.25-1.82); service personnel OR 1.74 (1.41-2.14) vs clinical staff
interpretation: MetS prevalence varied by employment category; psychosocial well-being was poorer with MetS

title: Dietary intake and prevalence of metabolic syndrome among tanker truck drivers in Ghana
key_effect_estimate: MetS 19.6%; age OR 1.3 p=0.04; HbA1c OR 9.6 p=0.004; SBP OR 1.2 p=0.01; service years OR 0.8 p=0.01
interpretation: MetS was common among tanker drivers; diet quality/energy inadequacy was notable

title: Correlation analysis between occupational stress and metabolic syndrome in workers of a petrochemical enterprise: based on two assessment models of occupational stress
key_effect_estimate: No overall association between occupational stress and MetS; adjusted models found D/C ratio negatively associated with SBP, social support negatively associated with waist circumference, and over-commitment positively associated with fasting blood glucose
interpretation: Occupational stress was not associated with MetS overall, but selected stress dimensions were associated with specific MetS components

title: Association Between Adequacy and Moderation of Quality of Diet with Metabolic Syndrome Parameters Among Iranian Health Workers Based on the Baseline Data of Employees Health Cohort Study
key_effect_estimate: MetS prevalence 22.3%; diet moderation associated with MetS OR 1.03 (95% CI 1.008-1.05), abdominal obesity OR 1.02 (1.003-1.04), elevated TG OR 1.02 (1.00-1.03), elevated FBS OR 1.03 (1.005-1.05)
interpretation: Diet moderation score was associated with MetS and several components; adequacy was not

title: Effectiveness of a canteen-based dietary intervention for metabolic syndrome in occupational men: A randomized controlled trial
main_caution: Unit of randomization/concealment and clustering need confirmation
interpretation: Canteen-based healthy lunch plus advice improved several MetS components

title: Dietary pattern and night work: metabolic syndrome in healthcare workers
key_effect_estimate: Night-shift workers had higher blood pressure, lower HDL cholesterol and 135% greater likelihood of MetS; shorter eating window linked to 7% lower MetS risk
interpretation: Night work and meal timing were associated with adverse metabolic risk

title: Prevalence and Factors Associated with Metabolic Syndrome Among Heavy Industry Workers: A Cross-Sectional Study
key_effect_estimate: MetS prevalence 21.4%; obesity and abdominal obesity associated with approximately 3.06-3.42-fold higher odds
interpretation: Adiposity and nutritional status were strongly associated with MetS

title: Association between adherence to the Mediterranean diet and metabolic syndrome in workers at a multinational company in Madrid
key_effect_estimate: MetS prevalence 6.45%; Mediterranean-diet adherence OR 0.45 (95% CI 0.31-0.68)
interpretation: Higher Mediterranean-diet adherence was associated with lower MetS prevalence

title: Work stress, dietary patterns, and physical activity on metabolic and hepatic biomarkers among healthcare professionals in Ghana
key_effect_estimate: MetS prevalence 11.0%; western diet significantly associated with abdominal obesity
interpretation: Dietary pattern showed clearer association than stress/activity

title: Association Between Dietary Patterns, Work Stress, Physical Activity, and Cardiometabolic Markers Among University Workers in Ghana
key_effect_estimate: High-protein dietary pattern and hypertension: aOR 1.869 (95% CI 1.011-3.455)
interpretation: Diet pattern associated with blood pressure; stress and PA not significantly associated with markers

title: Work stress, dietary patterns and metabolic syndrome among military personnel in Ghana: a cross-sectional study
key_effect_estimate: Work stress and MetS: OR 6.472 (95% CI 1.535-27.292)
interpretation: Work stress associated with higher MetS odds; estimate imprecise

title: Evaluation of a Voluntary Worksite Weight Loss Program on Metabolic Syndrome
interpretation: Voluntary worksite weight-loss program reduced MetS prevalence and risk factors

title: Effect of a Worksite-based Dietary Intervention Program for the Management of Metabolic Syndrome
exposure_domain: Dietary intervention and worksite food environment
key_effect_estimate: High-risk group improved weight, BMI, waist circumference, blood pressure, HDL and HbA1c; median MetS components decreased 3.0 to 1.0
interpretation: Worksite dietary intervention improved multiple MetS indicators in the high-risk group

title: Program Development and Effectiveness of Workplace Health Promotion Program for Preventing Metabolic Syndrome among Office Workers
sample_or_followup: 565 office workers in final analyses across intervention groups
key_effect_estimate: Targeted intensive group: waist 89.96 to 86.93 cm and fasting glucose 93.44 to 84.56 mg/dL, p<0.001; MetS prevalence 41.5% to 31.7%
interpretation: Targeted proactive workplace program improved MetS indicators; voluntary low-intensity components did not

title: Web-based high-intensity interval training with calorie restriction for workplace metabolic-syndrome
key_effect_estimate: Weight, blood pressure and triglycerides improved post-intervention and remained improved at 1 year (p<0.01)
interpretation: Web-based HIIT + calorie restriction improved MetS-related outcomes

title: A healthy lifestyle education intervention for metabolic syndrome risk reduction among office workers in Ethiopia: a single-blind, randomised controlled trial
exposure_domain: Lifestyle education: diet/physical activity/stress and other risk factors
main_caution: Masking target, concealment, attrition/ITT need confirmation
key_effect_estimate: Waist -5.33 cm; SBP -6.96 mmHg; DBP -4.21 mmHg; total cholesterol -34.12 mg/dL; LDL -20.68 mg/dL; all p<0.0001
interpretation: Workplace lifestyle education improved several MetS risk factors

title: Effects of an internet-based lifestyle intervention on cardio-metabolic risks and stress in Korean workers with metabolic syndrome: a controlled trial
main_caution: Nonrandomized allocation; only one pre- and one post-intervention measurement; follow-up completeness unclear
key_effect_estimate: Weight p=0.022; visceral fat p=0.033; waist circumference p=0.037
interpretation: Internet-based activity/diet/counselling improved selected cardiometabolic risks

title: Effects of a T'ai Chi-Based Health Promotion Program on Metabolic Syndrome Markers, Health Behaviors, and Quality of Life in Middle-Aged Male Office Workers: A Randomized Trial
main_caution: 37% attrition and completer analysis; allocation concealment not fully established
key_effect_estimate: SBP p=0.003; DBP p=0.037; triglycerides p=0.019
interpretation: T'ai Chi plus health education improved blood pressure and triglycerides

title: Relationships between occupational, leisure-time and commuting physical activity and metabolic syndrome among Taiwanese workers
main_caution: Cross-sectional temporality; physical activity self-reported and measurement validity not fully established
key_effect_estimate: High vs low leisure-time PA: OR 0.76 (95% CI 0.62-0.95)
interpretation: Higher leisure-time PA associated with lower MetS odds; commuting PA not associated

title: Effectiveness of a physical activity program on weight, physical fitness, occupational stress, job satisfaction and quality of life of overweight employees in high-tech industries: a randomized controlled study
main_caution: Allocation concealment, assessor blinding, attrition handling and analysis-by-randomization unclear
key_effect_estimate: Reduced number of MetS risk factors; lower triglycerides, total cholesterol and LDL
interpretation: Worksite PA program improved metabolic and fitness outcomes

title: Stress-buffering effects of physical activity and cardiorespiratory fitness on metabolic syndrome in police officers
main_caution: Participants not required to be MetS-free at baseline; follow-up/attrition handling incompletely reported
key_effect_estimate: Cardiorespiratory fitness predicting MetS risk: beta -0.38
interpretation: Higher fitness predicted lower follow-up MetS risk; no main effect for PA or work stress

title: Effects of a Remote Physical Activity Improvement Program on Male Office Workers with Metabolic Syndrome in Their 30s and 40s with Sedentary Behavior: A Randomized Controlled Trial
main_caution: Concealment, assessor blinding, attrition and ITT details unclear from accessible report
sample_or_followup: 75 male office workers with MetS; 12 weeks
key_effect_estimate: Intervention improved physical and physiological indicators versus control (P<0.05)
interpretation: Remote workplace PA education improved MetS-related indicators
